correctness.rationale: The exact statement is D_5=5 and D_7=6 for the affine F_p^2 torus under pair-line covering. For s<=4, at most s+C(s,2)(p-2) points are covered, giving 22<25 and 34<49. For a five-point set in F_7^2, a collinear triple leaves at most 4+7*5=39 external points covered (<44). For a five-point arc, the 10 secants each contribute 5 external incidences (50 total); among their 15 endpoint-disjoint line pairs at most eight are parallel because there are eight directions and each has at most two arc-secants. At least seven nonparallel intersections lie outside S and are at distinct points (at most two secants through any external point), so at most 50-7=43 external points are covered, whereas 44 are needed. The two displayed explicit witnesses were independently re-evaluated with exact modular bitmasks; their pair-lines cover all 25 or 49 points. A separately implemented complete enumeration of C(49,5)=1,906,884 five-subsets found no dominator; this checks the finite classification but is not the basis for the structural lower-bound proof.
residual_risks: No classification is asserted for primes other than 5 and 7.
The independent finite census alone would not establish a general prime-order theorem; the stated analytical proof is specifically for p=7.

evidence: The primary torus paper gives size bounds rather than exact D_5 and D_7; the four-point construction applies to even orders or multiples of three, not primes 5 or 7.
General projective saturating-set upper bounds operate in PG(2,q), not the affine torus, and do not supply both precise minimum values.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither an asymptotic bound nor projective coverage automatically specializes to the exact affine optima. Checked theorems and domains rather than only their titles.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge originality for two exact values in the same affine-torus geometric domination invariant as Aichholzer–Eppstein–Hainzl. That paper states general lower and upper bounds, plus four-point constructions for other orders, and asks for exact torus values; its inspected statements do not yield D_5=5 or D_7=6. No-three-in-line studies maximum point counts under a prohibition on collinearity, rather than minimum pair-secant domination. Projective 1-saturating-set surveys and tables concern PG(2,q), including the line at infinity; their tabulated parameters are not the affine covering number, and do not directly imply either exact affine value. Three Resultary semantic searches found no statement-equivalent or dominating published record. This is a bounded priority assessment, not proof of global novelty.
residual_risks: Best-of-knowledge originality is not certified global priority; niche finite-geometry census or differently named affine 1-saturating set classification could contain these values.
Projective small-q classification might have uninspected auxiliary affine lemmas even though its stated table is not directly equivalent.

checked_sources: Aichholzer–Eppstein–Hainzl, arXiv:2203.13170, conclusion asks for exact domination values.
Assigned RESULT.md explicit sharp witnesses and structural obstruction for p=7.
Independent exhaustive exact arithmetic p=7 classification used to corroborate p=7 lower bound.
value.rationale: The discrete-torus geometric domination number is the natural minimum size of a point set whose pair-secants cover the finite affine plane, and its exact evaluation is explicitly motivated as an open direction in the primary definition paper. The two first odd prime cases outside the composite four-point family have distinct sharp answers, D_5=5 and D_7=6, and p=7 requires a nontrivial forced secant-intersection obstruction. The exact pair supplies motivated finite calibration instances for incidence bounds, secant-cover algorithms and further classification; no general-prime breakthrough is claimed or required for these exact natural values.
residual_risks: Contribution is restricted to two small prime orders and does not improve asymptotic general-prime bounds.
Possible hidden earlier exact-value table would undermine value as a novel contribution.

limitations: Only F_5^2 and F_7^2 are classified; no general p formula or asymptotic claim.
The original verification program was inspected but not executed; a distinct exact program checked the witnesses and all p=7 five-subsets.
